qualifying_findings.title: GitHub Copilot local sandboxing generally available
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub made local sandboxing generally available for Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and VS Code Agent Host sessions, with policy controls for filesystem, network, credentials, local MCP, language servers, and enterprise-managed settings.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Local agent adoption guidance should treat sandbox policy as a first-class operating control, independent of model selection, especially for tool execution, credential access, and local MCP boundaries.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication_or_routing_no: Route broad Copilot and MXC product facts upstream; retain the local lens on sandbox policy, credential/network constraints, and MCP tool isolation.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Consider whether governance-and-risk/destructive-command-controls or retrieval-and-tools/tool-call-and-mcp-governance should later mention local sandbox policy as a reusable acceptance gate.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub purpose-built model for leaked secret detection
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub described a fine-tuned secret-detection model for AI-detected alerts, future push protection checks, and Copilot /security-review checks; it also noted AI Credit usage, administrator policy controls, and that agents should not enable credit-consuming capabilities or alter policies without explicit authorization.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Security-review workflows for coding agents need explicit authorization and budget controls before agent-initiated security checks or remediations become part of normal development loops.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication_or_routing_no: Route product availability and billing details upstream; keep the local rule that agents need explicit approval before enabling credit-consuming checks, changing policies, or applying security fixes.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub local model discovery in Copilot CLI
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub added /model discovery for supported models from a local Ollama instance in Copilot CLI 1.0.94-0, requiring explicit add/use confirmation and noting that local model selection does not automatically disable telemetry or remote provider traffic.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Local-model workflows still require provider, telemetry, offline-mode, and network-boundary checks; the presence of a local runtime is not proof of private or offline operation.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication_or_routing_no: Route product feature details upstream; retain the local operating-model caveat that local model routing needs explicit privacy, telemetry, and endpoint review.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub agent activity metrics attribution fix
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub said some IDE-based Copilot agent activity was undercounted or misattributed after SDK changes, that affected historical data cannot be backfilled, and that reliable metrics depend on current IDE/plugin versions, telemetry, network access to telemetry endpoints, and server-side fallbacks.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent adoption dashboards and cost/usage analyses should record client-version and telemetry gaps instead of treating vendor metrics as complete ground truth.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication_or_routing_no: Route IDE and Copilot product details upstream; keep the local implication for agent telemetry hygiene and adoption measurement caveats.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub stacked pull requests generally available
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub made stacked pull requests generally available, adding review and merge improvements such as preserved approvals for unchanged rebases, signed replacement commits, stack context visibility, lifecycle events, webhook signals, and GitHub CLI worktree support.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Coding-agent output can be easier to review when large changes are split into narrow dependent PRs with explicit stack navigation and lifecycle evidence.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication_or_routing_no: Route product details upstream; retain local relevance for fix-branch packaging, agent PR review ergonomics, and dependent-change decomposition.

qualifying_findings.title: JetBrains framework for reviewing AI-generated code
qualifying_findings.visible_date: October 2026; crawled within run window with no more precise visible article date in extracted page
qualifying_findings.summary: JetBrains Research described a participatory design study and survey on reviewing AI-generated code, framing trust calibration as the core problem and proposing overview, zoom/filter, and details-on-demand review support rather than line-by-line diff review alone.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: AI code review practice should expose risk and confidence signals at the granularity reviewers actually use, especially when agents generate larger multi-file changes.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication_or_routing_no: Route broad JetBrains entity coverage upstream; retain the local review-practice lens only if direct date evidence is accepted during ingest.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Because the extracted page showed month-level date only, treat this as lower-confidence and recheck direct visible publication metadata before ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: Seapoint office-desktop coding agent workflow
qualifying_findings.summary: Seapoint described an in-house coding-agent system running on an office desktop with repository-stored guides, prompts, and skills, per-task git workspaces, sandboxed Docker VMs, egress rules, mock services, dummy data, browser-based verification loops, screenshots, videos, preview URLs, and human plan/code review.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The practice pattern combines shared durable context, isolated workspaces, runtime evidence, manual override paths, and on-call review into a concrete agent-fleet operating model.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication_or_routing_no: Route product and vendor background upstream; keep the downstream practice pattern for shared prompts/skills, sandboxed workspaces, evidence artifacts, and review handoffs.

qualifying_findings.title: Anchor Sprint review stack for agent-written code
qualifying_findings.summary: Anchor Sprint argued that agent-written code needs layered checks before a human signs off, naming risks such as unvetted dependencies, injection, secrets, and access-control flaws, and emphasizing that a person remains responsible for approval.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent-code review guidance should separate automated reading from final approval, preserve segregation of duties, and watch package-install and access-control risk in generated changes.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication_or_routing_no: Route vendor/product claims upstream; retain local approval-boundary, segregation-of-duties, and package-install-risk implications.

qualifying_findings.title: Optimal AI safer CLI agent mode and source review stats
qualifying_findings.summary: Optimal AI's changelog says review statistics now separate CLI, IDE, and MCP review sources, the CLI shows the limit that applies to the user, and agent mode protects sensitive files.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Review systems that run through CLI, IDE, and MCP surfaces need source-level accounting, visible limits, and sensitive-file controls for agent activity.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication_or_routing_no: Route product coverage upstream; keep the local accounting/control pattern for multi-surface review agents.

qualifying_findings.title: Deska weekly review ritual for agent-shipped work
qualifying_findings.summary: Deska proposed a weekly audit ritual for AI-assisted developers, focusing on agent diffs, architectural drift, context verification, dependency review, and documentation alignment.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Teams using multiple agent sessions need periodic architectural review outside the immediate PR diff to catch drift, duplicated logic, unapproved packages, and instruction failures.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication_or_routing_no: Route product references upstream; retain the local recurring audit practice and context-verification implication.

qualifying_findings.title: DETENT software audit trail for agent-made changes
qualifying_findings.summary: DETENT argued that an audit trail for agent-written software should preserve original intent, task contract, diff, system-run verification, outcome, and a named timestamped human approval, while treating agent session logs as debugging material rather than durable evidence.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Governance pages should distinguish session transcripts from tamper-resistant delivery evidence and require human signatures at release boundaries.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication_or_routing_no: Route vendor background upstream; retain the local audit-trail pattern, evidence package boundary, and named human approval requirement.

qualifying_findings.title: Appy Pie comparison of vibe, agentic, and spec-driven coding
qualifying_findings.visible_date: Last updated on October 8, 2026; test dated 8 Oct 2026
qualifying_findings.summary: Appy Pie compared one feature built three ways and reported that a spec-driven run passed all hidden checks faster than the agentic run, while the agentic run performed many checks but changed a behavior the authors had not requested.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Verification should be anchored to human-written acceptance criteria; agent self-checks can prove the code satisfies the agent's interpretation rather than the intended behavior.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication_or_routing_no: Route tool/product background upstream; keep the local implication for executable specifications, acceptance criteria, and check interpretation.

qualifying_findings.title: Start Debugging explanation of GitHub Agentic Workflows
qualifying_findings.summary: Start Debugging described GitHub Agentic Workflows as a Markdown-to-Actions compiler with YAML frontmatter for trigger, permissions, engine, tools, and allowed outputs, running agents in read-only network-firewalled jobs and applying writes through permission-scoped jobs after threat detection.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent workflow artifacts can be treated as declarative contracts that compile into constrained CI execution, separating agent reasoning from write authority and output promotion.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication_or_routing_no: Route product/entity facts upstream; retain the downstream pattern of declarative agent workflows, permission-scoped writes, and safe output promotion.
